ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: The problem states that the solution set of the inequality ax-b<0 is (1,+∞). The critical point of the linear inequality ax-b<0 is ax-b=0, namely x=b/a. Its solution set is on the right side of the critical point, indicating that a<0, and b/a=1, so b=a. Substituting b=a into the target inequality (ax+b)(x-3)>0 gives (ax+a)(x-3)>0, namely a(x+1)(x-3)>0. Because a<0, after dividing both sides by the negative number a, the direction of the inequality changes, obtaining (x+1)(x-3)<0. The two zeros of this product are -1 and 3, and when the product is less than 0, x is between the two roots, so the solution set is (-1,3).

method.method_draft: Read the text statement: the solution set of ax-b<0 is (1,+∞). For a linear inequality ax-b<0 to hold to the right of its zero, the coefficient must satisfy a<0, and the zero is x=b/a=1, so b=a. Substitute b=a into the target inequality: (ax+b)(x-3)>0 becomes a(x+1)(x-3)>0. Since a<0, divide by the negative constant and reverse the sign to get (x+1)(x-3)<0. Use the rule that a quadratic product with roots -1 and 3 is negative between the roots, giving x∈(-1,3).

method.method_draft: Read from the text that ax-b<0 switches sign at x=1 and is negative for all x>1. Interpret y=ax-b as a line: because it is negative to the right of its zero, its slope a is negative. The zero condition at x=1 gives a-b=0, hence b=a. Instead of fully solving parameters, use this to locate the zero of ax+b: ax+b=ax+a=a(x+1), so its zero is x=-1. Since a<0, ax+b is positive on the left of -1 and negative on the right of -1. Combine this sign pattern with x-3, which is negative for x<3 and positive for x>3. Make a sign chart over intervals (-∞,-1), (-1,3), (3,+∞); the product is positive only on (-1,3).
